presentation.purpose: Transform each number independently into a smooth score between zero and one. Zero becomes one half. Shape and row order stay the same; no learned weights or axis settings.

learning.title: Explore Sigmoid in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Transform hidden features independently, then learn two final class scores.
learning.formula: Zero becomes 0.5; larger inputs approach 1 and smaller inputs approach 0.
paragraphs: Sigmoid changes each number separately. It does not make a row sum to one.
Use the example to inspect its hidden feature scores. The final Linear still produces raw class scores for the training rule.
Large positive or negative inputs change their scores very little. This can make learning slower. A score between zero and one is not automatically a trustworthy probability.

presentation.purpose: Transform each number independently into a smooth signed value between minus one and one. Zero stays zero. Shape and row order stay the same; no learned weights or axis settings.

learning.title: Explore Tanh in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Keep the sign of hidden features, then learn two final class scores.
learning.formula: Zero stays zero; larger positive inputs approach 1 and negative inputs approach −1.
paragraphs: Tanh changes each number separately. A negative input stays negative, and a positive input stays positive.
Inspect the hidden values in this editable example. The final Linear produces raw class scores for training.
Very large input magnitudes change the output only a little. This flattening, called saturation, can slow learning. Tanh does not turn a row into probabilities.

presentation.purpose: Replace each negative number with zero and preserve each positive number. Zero stays zero. Shape and row order stay the same; no learned weights or axis settings. This operation does not mutate its input.

learning.title: Explore ReLU in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Clip negative hidden features to zero, then learn final class scores.
learning.formula: Negative inputs become 0; positive inputs and zero stay unchanged.
paragraphs: ReLU changes each number separately. It does not mix columns or make a row sum to one.
Inspect the hidden values in this editable example. The final Linear still produces raw class scores for training.
Negative inputs produce zero and have zero small-change sensitivity. A feature that stays negative may stop contributing to learning. The original input is preserved for other branches.

presentation.purpose: Smoothly weight each number using its value. Choose exact or tanh approximation. Shape and row order stay the same; no learned weights.

learning.title: Explore GELU in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Smoothly weight hidden features, then learn final class scores.
learning.formula: Negative values are reduced smoothly; larger positive values mostly pass through.
paragraphs: GELU changes each number separately. Some negative outputs remain negative, unlike ReLU clipping.
Choose exact mode or the tanh approximation in Configuration. Both implement a smooth gate; the approximation uses a slightly different calculation.
Inspect hidden feature values in the editable example. The final Linear still produces raw class scores for training.

presentation.purpose: Turn each chosen group of scores into shares that sum to one. Other directions and observation order stay unchanged.

learning.title: Explore Softmax in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Compare chosen groups of hidden scores, then learn final class scores.
learning.formula: Each selected group sums to one; a larger score receives a larger share.
paragraphs: The normalization axis chooses which numbers compete within each observation. Choose the last direction with −1 or another sample direction by its position.
Softmax mixes scores inside each chosen group. Changing one score changes the shares of the others. It never mixes separate observations.
Inspect group shares in this editable example. The final Linear still produces raw class scores for training; these hidden shares alone do not prove a prediction is reliable.

presentation.purpose: Learn how strongly negative measurements contribute.

learning.title: Explore PReLU in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Learn how strongly negative measurements contribute.
learning.disclosureTitle: How this block changes a measurement
learning.formula: Learn how strongly negative measurements contribute.
paragraphs: A tensor is an array with named directions. A sample is one observation; a batch is a group of observations. PReLU keeps positive values and multiplies negative values by a learned slope. A slope is an adjustable multiplier, not a new input direction.

Slope count 1 shares one multiplier. To learn a separate multiplier for each channel, match Slope count to the first sample direction. A channel is a separate measurement field; it is not automatically the final column direction. Initial slope sets each starting multiplier.

Each block owns its learned slopes. Training updates those values; cloning creates another owner and connecting one block to several destinations reuses its same slopes. Use the shared-slope and channel-slope lessons to edit the supplied parameters and measure output, input influence and slope influence. Input influence describes how a small input change affects a result.

presentation.purpose: Compare sample scores on a compressed logarithmic scale.

learning.title: Explore LogSoftmax in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Compare sample scores on a compressed logarithmic scale.
learning.disclosureTitle: How this block changes a measurement
learning.formula: Compare sample scores on a compressed logarithmic scale.
paragraphs: Input scores express relative preferences. A probability is a share between zero and one; normalized shares sum to one along the chosen direction. LogSoftmax records these shares on a logarithmic scale, a compressed scale that represents multiplication as addition. Its output values are not a probability table.

A tensor is an array with named directions. A sample is one observation; a batch is a group of observations. Normalization direction selects the sample values to compare. Keep the observation direction separate; a negative direction counts backward from the last direction.

Open the example to inspect scores and logarithmic output values. The measured lesson checks both the values and input influence: how a small change affects a result. Large score shifts are handled by a stable calculation; extremely distant values can still produce arithmetic that must be refused.

presentation.purpose: Temporarily hide selected values during training, then keep every value for evaluation.

learning.title: Explore Dropout in a classifier
learning.subtitle: Temporarily hide selected values during training, then keep every value for evaluation.
learning.disclosureTitle: How this block changes a measurement
learning.formula: Temporarily hide selected values during training, then keep every value for evaluation.
paragraphs: Dropout temporarily hides a randomly selected portion of values while a model trains. Drop probability 0.5 hides about half over many observations, not exactly half in every call. Retained values are scaled upward to keep their average contribution comparable.

A tensor is an array with named directions; a batch is a group of observations. This block follows the model’s training or evaluation mode. In evaluation it keeps every value and draws no new random pattern. Probability 0 keeps everything during training; probability 1 hides everything during training.

New calls draw new patterns. A run seed can repeat the same call schedule on the same runtime and device; CPU and Apple GPU patterns need not match. The two measured lessons compare training and evaluation behavior. Input influence means how a small input change affects a result. Seeds and modes belong to the run or lesson rather than hidden block controls.
